intro: Picture this: you wake up, open the curtains, and soft morning light slides through a big glass wall onto green rice fields with a far line of mountains. A few hundred metres' walk away stands the golden Phra That Chae Haeng, the year-of-the-rabbit stupa and one of Nan's most revered landmarks — Pagoda Sight Residence is a small, loft-style 2-star boutique hotel with just 7–8 rooms in the Ban Nong Tao community, Muang Tued Subdistrict, Phu Phiang District, Nan · what real reviews agree on most is the peace and quiet, the field and mountain views, and an owner who looks after guests personally, warmly and without fuss · the building is designed with roughly 3-metre ceilings and large glass walls that open onto the natural scenery, plus a garden, free private parking, and a shared lounge to sit and relax · from about THB 1,200/night, rated around 9.0 from real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor

body.html: Who Pagoda Sight Residence suits — the big picture — to put it as simply as possible, Pagoda Sight Residence is a place for people coming to Nan for quiet, a slower pace, and a stay near Phra That Chae Haeng rather than for luxury or a full set of facilities · it isn't a big hotel in town within walking distance of Khuang Mueang and the walking street, and it isn't a resort with a pool and a spa · it's a small loft-style boutique hotel that the owner deliberately built with only 7–8 rooms, in the Ban Nong Tao community, Muang Tued Subdistrict, Phu Phiang District, on the far side of the Nan River from town · the whole idea is right there in the name — "Pagoda Sight," the spot where you can see the stupa — because it sits within walking distance of Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, the birth-year stupa for those born in the year of the rabbit and one of the must-stop landmarks for anyone visiting Nan · the building is designed in a Homey Loft style with roughly 3-metre ceilings and large glass walls that open onto views of rice fields and mountains, giving an airy, open feel that sits close to nature · real reviews line up on who this place fits: couples who want a quiet, romantic atmosphere, slow travellers who like waking up to a field view, merit-makers who want to stay near Phra That Chae Haeng, and people who drive here themselves and value quiet above all · for anyone who wants to stay in town within walking distance of cafés and the walking street, wants a pool, or isn't driving themselves, this may not be the answer, and a hotel in central Nan is worth considering instead · you could say Pagoda Sight plays the "quiet stay near the stupa, on a reasonable budget" angle pretty clearly, and it's a positioning that matches the slow charm of Nan rather well

Location and getting around — Pagoda Sight Residence sits at 441 Moo 3, Muang Tued Subdistrict, Phu Phiang District, in the Ban Nong Tao community, a quiet neighbourhood on the far side of the Nan River from town · the strength of the location is how close it is — within walking distance of a major temple: only about 340–400 metres from Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, an easy walk to pay respects and see the golden stupa, and it's also close to natural areas such as Chae Haeng Forest Park, under half a kilometre away · the honest point to make is that this is not in central Nan — it's about 3–4 kilometres, or roughly 8–12 min drive, from the centre of town, including Khuang Mueang Nan, Wat Phumin and the Kad Khuang Mueang walking street · that's not far if you have a car, but it's too far to walk and you'll need a vehicle every time you want to head into town · getting in from further afield is convenient, though: it's only about 6–7 kilometres from Nan Nakhon Airport (NNT), or roughly 10–15 min drive, so if you fly into Nan and want to reach your room quickly, this location has the edge · for driving out to sights around the area such as Wat Sri Panton, Sao Din Na Noi, or the route up to Doi Phu Kha–Bo Kluea, central Nan makes a convenient starting point · the point to state clearly, in line with real reviews, is that this place is most convenient when you have your own car or a rental · without a car, public transport is hard to rely on, and you'll need to call a taxi or a hired car into town, with fares that add up (some reviews note a fare of around 100 baht each way into town) — that's something to weigh up before booking

"Really peaceful stay. I opened the curtains in the morning to a view of fields and mountains, and it was an easy walk over to Phra That Chae Haeng. The owner is lovely and runs it personally, very friendly. The room was clean, spacious, nice atmosphere — perfect for a slow, restful trip."

Room types and decor — Pagoda Sight is a small place with around 7–8 rooms (the number varies slightly between booking platforms over time), designed in a Homey Loft style that leans into an airy, open feel · what sets it apart from the usual small stay is the roughly 3-metre ceilings and large glass walls that open onto views of rice fields and mountains, which make the rooms bright and feel larger than they are · there are several room types, starting with the Standard Queen / Twin at roughly 35 sqm for couples or two friends · stepping up is the Deluxe Room with Private Balcony at roughly 40 sqm, with a private balcony looking out to the mountains — the room many reviews mention for its view · and the largest is the two-bedroom Family Suite at roughly 100 sqm for families or groups of friends · in-room amenities include air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with cable, a minibar, coffee maker, kettle, a private bathroom with shower and hairdryer, toiletries, a wardrobe, and some rooms have a kitchenette with microwave, handy for longer stays · plenty of reviews agree that the rooms are clean, spacious, nicely decorated, and the view from the room is very good · but to be straight about it, the point raised most often about the rooms is that the mattress is fairly firm — some international reviews say outright that the mattress was firm enough to be uncomfortable and gave them a sore back, which comes down to differing sleep preferences · people who like a firm mattress may be happy, but anyone who prefers a soft one should know this in advance and ask about the mattress / a topper when booking if it matters to them

Facilities and atmosphere — the first thing to make clear is that Pagoda Sight Residence is a small boutique hotel that sells atmosphere and quiet first, with no swimming pool, gym or spa, so if your main aim is to swim or use the full facilities of a big resort, this may not be the fit · what Pagoda Sight does have, and does well, is relaxed shared spaces — a garden, a shared lounge for sitting and sipping coffee, and a terrace deck looking out over fields and mountains that fits the rural surroundings nicely · there's a small in-house restaurant/café and a snack bar for drinks and light bites, room service within the limits of a small place, and a car rental service for those who want to head out around Nan · the real strength is free private parking, which matters a lot for a location that requires a car, plus 24-hour reception · Wi-Fi is free, especially in the shared areas · the honest note from real reviews is that the Wi-Fi signal drops or is unstable at times, and because the property sits next to greenery and rice fields, ants or insects can sometimes wander in, as is natural for a rural stay · it's fair to say the facilities here are "small but just right for a peaceful break" rather than an all-in-one stay, but for anyone who comes to sleep somewhere quiet near the stupa and spend time with the natural views, what's on offer is enough and fits the slow pace of Nan

Food and what to eat nearby — Pagoda Sight has a small in-house restaurant/café and a snack bar, and breakfast is the one thing to read the fine print on, because booking platforms note that breakfast isn't included in the standard room across every package — some channels and packages include it, others charge extra, so check carefully when booking · what's worth noting is that many real reviews from guests who did get breakfast speak well of it, saying breakfast is tasty and freshly made by the owner, which is part of the charm of a small owner-run place · for other meals, since the property sits in a community on the Phu Phiang side where eateries aren't as dense as in town, having a car helps a lot — drive into central Nan in about 8–12 minutes and you'll find local restaurants, cafés and well-known dishes such as Nan-style khao soi, noodles, and plenty of good coffee shops, especially around Wat Phumin and the Kad Khuang Mueang walking street that runs on Friday–Saturday–Sunday evenings · around the property itself there are a fair few eateries and convenience stores in the community, but they aren't dense, so if you want late-night food or specific items, it's best to stock up during the day · overall, food isn't the reason to come and eat in-house at Pagoda Sight, but the owner's home-made breakfast is a nice bonus done well, while the real stars for other meals are the restaurants and cafés of Nan, a few minutes' drive away

Service — service is the point that earns the most consistent praise in real reviews of Pagoda Sight, and it's the heart of this small place's charm · because it's an owner-run stay, many reviews mention the owner and team as warm, friendly and attentive, happy to recommend places to visit, restaurants, and driving routes around Nan · being small turns into an advantage here, in that guests get close, personal care — like staying at a relative's house — with no long queues and a lot of privacy · TripAdvisor rates this place highly for service and cleanliness (many give full marks), which fits the overall picture that the strength here is the "people" and the care · to be straight about it, the limitation to be aware of is that, as a small place without a large team, some services are simple and scaled to the property rather than the full standard service of a chain hotel, and confirming details in advance (especially breakfast and check-in times) will help the trip go smoothly · overall, service at Pagoda Sight is its real selling point and the reason many people are impressed enough to want to return

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent, with high scores (Trip.com around 9.4, Booking.com around 8.9, and TripAdvisor around 4.2 out of 5) · on the praise side: the most-mentioned point is the peace and quiet and the natural setting — field and mountain views from the rooms and shared spaces, the privacy, and the relaxed, slow feel · next come the owner and the warm, friendly service that almost every review brings up, the cleanliness of the rooms that scores highly, rooms that are spacious and bright thanks to the high ceilings and large glass walls, the location within walking distance of Phra That Chae Haeng, free parking, and the owner's home-made breakfast that many praise · on the watch-out side: the point raised most clearly is the firm mattress — some reviews say the mattress was firm enough to be uncomfortable and give a sore back, dragging the sleep-quality score down in a few reviews · next come a location that requires a car, since it's about 3–4 kilometres out of town and you need to call a car in (a fare of around 100 baht each way), a Wi-Fi signal that drops at times, ants or insects getting into the room occasionally because it sits next to greenery, a few people mentioning the odd small stain on the sheets at times, and value that some reviews rate as middling depending on whether the sleep style suits them or not · most of these gripes are more about setting expectations correctly (a small rural stay that sells quiet and views, not an all-round town hotel) than big problems that keep people from returning

"Clean room, lovely field view, the owner is so kind. My only gripes are that the mattress is fairly firm for us, and you need a car to get into town. Next time I'll ask about the mattress first, but the peace and quiet is great value for the price."

Price and value — the starting price for a Standard room is around THB 1,200/night in the normal range, rising with room type and season, with the Deluxe room with balcony and the two-bedroom Family Suite running higher, up to around THB 3,600 for the larger room or in high season · compared with stays in the same area and in central Nan, this price is accessible and good value among small boutique hotels selling atmosphere, cleanliness, and owner-run service, especially once you factor in the field and mountain views, the high ceilings and glass walls, free parking, and a location within walking distance of Phra That Chae Haeng · Nan has stays at all levels, from budget hostels and old-town guesthouses to small boutique resorts along the Nan River — Pagoda Sight sits in the small, mid-priced boutique group where the selling point isn't luxury or facilities, but a quiet atmosphere and close, personal care · if you're planning to come to Nan for a slow, restful trip, drive around the area, pay respects at Phra That Chae Haeng, and value quiet over in-town convenience, the money you spend on Pagoda Sight buys back atmosphere and care in full · but if your main aim is to walk around the old town every day without driving, or you want a soft mattress and a full set of facilities, the value may drop, so weigh it up against your own trip style

Good to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · one, the mattress is what reviews mention most — if you like a soft mattress, ask about the firmness and request an extra topper when booking · two, the property is about 3–4 kilometres out of town, so it's most convenient with your own car or a rental; without a car, allow for the cost and time of calling a vehicle into town (around 100 baht each way) or use the property's car rental service · three, breakfast isn't included in every package, so check clearly when booking whether your chosen package includes it · four, the Wi-Fi drops at times, so if you need to work online on anything important, bring a backup mobile data SIM · five, because it sits next to greenery there may be the odd ant or insect, so keep food sealed and close doors and windows at night · six, the property has just 7–8 rooms and is a popular stay in the Phra That Chae Haeng area, so during Nan's high season (November–February, when it's cool and the sea of mist is lovely) rooms fill up fast — book ahead · seven, check-in is around 1:00 PM–8:00 PM and check-out is before 11:00 AM, so if you arrive outside those hours, let the owner know in advance

Summary — from everything real reviews say, Pagoda Sight Residence is the best fit for people coming to Nan for quiet, natural views, and a stay near Phra That Chae Haeng on a reasonable budget · the peace and quiet, the field and mountain views through the high glass walls, an owner who looks after guests personally and warmly, clean and spacious rooms, and a location within walking distance of Phra That Chae Haeng give it a charm of its own that fits the slow rhythm of Nan · but it's fair to admit this is a small boutique with no pool, a mattress that's fairly firm for some, Wi-Fi that drops at times, the odd insect as is natural for a rural stay, and a location that's most convenient with your own car · if you're after a town hotel within walking distance of cafés and the walking street, want a pool and a full set of facilities, or aren't driving yourself, this may not be the answer, and a stay in central Nan is worth considering instead · but for a trip where you want to wake up to a field view, walk over to the stupa, and use your stay as a small, quiet home base on the Phu Phiang side — Pagoda Sight Residence answers that with real charm and value, as long as you have a car, set your expectations right, and brace for a firm mattress in advance

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Pagoda Sight Residence Nan

faq.q: Where is Pagoda Sight Residence · is it far from central Nan?
faq.a: The property is at 441 Moo 3, Muang Tued Subdistrict, Phu Phiang District, Nan, in the Ban Nong Tao community · only about 340–400 metres from Wat Phra That Chae Haeng, within walking distance · but it's about 3–4 kilometres, or roughly 8–12 min drive, from central Nan (Wat Phumin / Khuang Mueang), and about 6–7 kilometres from Nan Nakhon Airport · this location is most convenient with your own car or a rental

faq.q: Who is Pagoda Sight Residence good for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, slow travellers, merit-makers who want to stay near Phra That Chae Haeng, and people who drive themselves and value peace and quiet · the highlights are the quiet atmosphere, field and mountain views through the high glass walls, and a warm, owner-run welcome · if you want to stay in town within walking distance of cafés and the walking street, want a pool, or aren't driving yourself, a stay in central Nan may suit you better

faq.q: How much does Pagoda Sight Residence cost to start · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from about THB 1,200/night for a Standard room of roughly 35 sqm · there's a Deluxe Room with Private Balcony of roughly 40 sqm with mountain views, and a two-bedroom Family Suite of roughly 100 sqm for families (up to around THB 3,600 for the larger room / in high season) · the property has just 7–8 rooms, so book ahead and compare across platforms

faq.q: Does Pagoda Sight Residence have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: It has no swimming pool, leaning instead on a quiet atmosphere, field and mountain views, a garden, and a shared lounge · as for breakfast, it's not included in every package — some channels/packages include it, others charge extra, so check the terms when booking · many real reviews from guests who got breakfast praise it as tasty and made by the owner

faq.q: What are the mattress and the sleep like at Pagoda Sight?
faq.a: The point reviews mention most about the rooms is a fairly firm mattress — some reviews say it was firm enough to be uncomfortable and gave a sore back, dragging the sleep-quality score down somewhat · it comes down to preference; people who like a firm mattress may be happy · we recommend asking about the mattress firmness and requesting an extra topper when booking if you like a soft mattress

faq.q: Do I need my own car to get to Pagoda Sight Residence?
faq.a: Not strictly, but your own car or a rental is most convenient, since the property is about 3–4 kilometres out of town on the Phu Phiang side and public transport is limited · the property has free private parking and a car rental service · without a car, you'll need to call a taxi or a hired vehicle into town (a fare of around 100 baht each way), so allow for the time and cost
